<!-- Modal 1 -->
<div class="modal fade" id="modal1" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="modal1label" aria-modal="true" role="dialog">
<div class="modal-dialog modal-lg">
<div class="modal-content">
<div class="modal-header opt1-header">
<h4 class="modal-title" id="modal1label"> Option 1: Allow AI With Disclosure</h4>
<button type="button" class="btn-close btn-close-white" data-bs-dismiss="modal" aria-label="Close"></button>
</div>
<div class="modal-body">
<p>Applicants can use AI tools but must clearly state how they used them.</p>
<p><strong>Pros:</strong> Efficiency when looking through resumes, encourages transparency.</p>
<p><strong>Cons:</strong> Loss of genuine creativity and critical thinking skills, errors and bias in resume screeners, leaving out potential candidates.</p>
<p><strong>Impact on Stakeholders:</strong> Applicants may feel pressured to use AI, HR must enforce disclosure rules, reviewers may still struggle to trust resumes.</p>
<hr>
<p><strong>Utilitarianism:</strong> May increase efficiency but could create inequality between applicants with and without AI access. Positive outcomes depend on whether transparency is actually enforced.</p>
<p><strong>Deontology:</strong> Requiring disclosure supports fairness and honesty, though enforcement may be difficult and some applicants may not follow the rule.</p>
<p><strong>Virtue Ethics:</strong> Encourages honesty and responsibility, but heavy AI reliance may reduce personal effort and creativity.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Modal 2 -->
<div class="modal fade" id="modal2" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="modal2label" aria-modal="true" role="dialog">
<div class="modal-dialog modal-lg">
<div class="modal-content">
<div class="modal-header opt2-header">
<h4 class="modal-title" id="modal2label"> Option 2: Allow AI for Grammar and Translation Only</h4>
<button type="button" class="btn-close btn-close-white" data-bs-dismiss="modal" aria-label="Close"></button>
</div>
<div class="modal-body">
<p>Applicants can use AI tools that help fix grammar and translate language that is hard to understand.</p>
<p><strong>Pros:</strong> Reduces overreliance on AI, enables AI as a support tool, maintains fairness while supporting accessibility.</p>
<p><strong>Cons:</strong> Might take more time to review each resume, hard to monitor how applicants used AI.</p>
<p><strong>Impact on Stakeholders:</strong> Applicants still benefit from AI support, HR has clearer guidelines, AI companies may see reduced use.</p>
<hr>
<p><strong>Utilitarianism:</strong> Balances efficiency and fairness. Especially benefits non-native English speakers while preserving critical thinking — likely produces the greatest overall benefit.</p>
<p><strong>Deontology:</strong> Follows a clear rule about acceptable AI use, promoting fairness while preventing misuse of AI-generated content.</p>
<p><strong>Virtue Ethics:</strong> Supports responsibility and self-development — applicants still reflect on and communicate their own experiences.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Modal 3 -->
<div class="modal fade" id="modal3" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="modal3label" aria-modal="true" role="dialog">
<div class="modal-dialog modal-lg">
<div class="modal-content">
<div class="modal-header opt3-header">
<h4 class="modal-title" id="modal3label"> Option 3: Do Not Allow AI</h4>
<button type="button" class="btn-close btn-close-white" data-bs-dismiss="modal" aria-label="Close"></button>
</div>
<div class="modal-body">
<p>Applicants and resume reviewers are not allowed to use AI at all.</p>
<p><strong>Pros:</strong> Allows human creativity and critical thinking, hirers can connect with applicants on a deeper level, ensures equal expectations.</p>
<p><strong>Cons:</strong> Increases workload for resume reviewers, disadvantages non-native speakers.</p>
<p><strong>Impact on Stakeholders:</strong> Heavy workload for resume reviewers, AI companies lose revenue from hiring-related services.</p>
<hr>
<p><strong>Utilitarianism:</strong> Protects creativity and authenticity but may disadvantage applicants with language barriers and increase reviewer workload.</p>
<p><strong>Deontology:</strong> Promotes equal treatment of all applicants, but may limit access to tools that support communication and accessibility.</p>
<p><strong>Virtue Ethics:</strong> Strongly supports independence, effort, and authenticity — individuals rely entirely on their own skills.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
